newsitem.title: USA: Drug stocks buoyant, Eli Lilly leads pack.
newsitem.headline: Drug stocks buoyant, Eli Lilly leads pack.

text.p: Shares of U.S. drug makers were robust on Monday, as positive sentiment related to Eli Lilly and Co's new anti-osteoporosis drug spilled over to boost stocks of other pharmaceutical companies, analysts said.

Last week, Lilly said results from trials of its anti-osteoporosis drug raloxifene, or Evista, showed that it increased bone mass while producing fewer side effects than the estrogen replacement therapy now used.
The news prompted Wall Street to nudge up its earnings outlook for Lilly, and other drug manufacturers were catching some of the enthusiasm, analysts said.

"This wonderful Evista story has triggered a surge in the drug group," said Christina Heuer, an analyst at Smith Barney. She reiterated her buy rating on Lilly and said last week's announcement had prompted analysts to raise estimates.
"We are seeing earnings continuing to uptick for the drug group and that's bullish for stock performance," she said. "New drug stories are leading the group."
Eli Lilly closed up 3-1/8 at 100-1/4, Merck and Co rose 1-1/4 at 93-1/2, Johnson & Johnson rose 1-1/2 at 61-5/8 and Pfizer Inc added 1-1/2 at 108-1/2.
Merck received FDA approval in 1995 for its Fosamax treatment for osteoporosis and other drugmakers have similar bisphosophonate therapy drugs in development.
"What we're seeing today in the drug sector is fallout from last week's osteoporosis meeting," James Keeney, an analyst at Rodman & Renshaw, said.
The industry's strong fundamentals are propelled by new products, which were boosting earnings estimates, Barbara Ryan, an analyst at Alex. Brown, said.
To be sure, other analysts said the drug sector was benefiting from investor rotation, and that there had been no major changes in the broad industry picture.

"I'm a bit surprised," George Sasic, an analyst at Dominick & Dominick, said. "The multiples are way up there. These are core holdings, which offer liquid, dependable sources of growth. There have been no change in fundamentals."
He said raloxifine was in the initial phases of market introduction and while it could prove to be a promising treatment, it still had to face the open market.
